chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When the Imam finishes (the prayer), one should not pray two rak'ahs in his place until he turns away from that place."

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The leader of the congregational prayer

ai.seo_question: When should one pray the two voluntary rak'ahs after the Imam finishes the congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the etiquette of transitioning from congregational prayer to individual Sunnah prayers, emphasizing the need to break the continuity of the Imam's specific station to avoid confusion or premature departure. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining distinct ritual phases and respecting the spatial dynamics of the prayer leader. The ruling underscores the importance of mindful transition in worship, ensuring that the congregational act is fully concluded before initiating personal devotions.
